topic: Will the periodic table ever be complete?

survey_agent.purpose: Define the evidence boundary, separate four meanings of completeness, and establish research gaps.

idea_agent.purpose: Search competing directions and select an evidence-aware conditional frontier rather than a final-number forecast.
idea_agent.selected_direction: D2 — Beyond Element 118: A Calibrated, Evidence-Aware Frontier for Conditional New-Element Reachability
idea_agent.rejected_direction: D4 — Single-number final atomic number forecast

experiment_design_agent.purpose: Specify a time-split, source-bound, non-operational protocol for conditional reachability assessment.

author_agent.purpose: Create a source-bound IEEE research proposal while retaining upstream uncertainty, abstention, and governance constraints.

core_conclusion: Element 118 is the current IUPAC-recognized institutional boundary, not a demonstrated physical endpoint. Future elements are not guaranteed by ingenuity alone because nuclear stability, fission, Coulomb effects, production and observation reachability, evidence quality, and IUPAC/IUPAP assessment remain distinct constraints.
human_review_required: Verify literature interpretation and source eligibility before using the corpus.
Have nuclear-physics and discovery-criteria experts approve the evidence codebook and adjudicate ambiguity.
Reserve discovery recognition, priority, and naming for IUPAC/IUPAP processes.
Obtain all facility, radiation, and institutional approvals before any physical experiment; this deliverable provides none.
known_limitations: No final atomic number is known or claimed.
The proposed model has not been executed or calibrated and provides no empirical result.
Sparse historical records and model disagreement may preclude reliable extrapolation.
Artifact traceability preserves claim boundaries but cannot establish physical truth.

validation.hash_check: Not performed; no deterministic-generation or file-transfer integrity claim required it.
